about: The one place that says what is built. Pages and the README read this file. A feature may be 'built' only if 'verify' (a command anyone can run) and 'proof' (a file in this repository) are filled in. To flip a feature: edit its status here, then run: python3 tools/site.py build && python3 tools/site.py sync-readme && python3 tools/site.py check

features.name: Memory that carries over
features.plain: A recorded run put a past job back in front of the next prompt, with a record of where it came from. Recall of a new, different job is a small preliminary test.
features.today: Setup, record and recall run from a fresh clone.
features.exists: Setup, record and recall run: `anima memory setup` prepares a local TRACE store; each `anima run --memory trace` records the run; `anima memory recall` returns similar past fixes, showing only hits re-checked against their source (one recorded fresh-clone run: 1 hit, similarity 0.67, source check OK). A separate small held-out check found 0 hits at 0.30 with the baseline passages; two tuned variants cleared 0.30 on 2 of 3 new tasks (preliminary).
features.limit: A small local store, not the 100-million-token library. Recall is only as good as the runs recorded. Recall of a new, different job is a small preliminary test (baseline 0 hits at 0.30 on 3 held-out tasks). Setup needs the network once.
features.verify: anima memory recall "statslite moving average should return one simple average for every full window"
features.needs: install, then anima memory setup (network once), then one anima run --memory trace to record a run

features.name: A checker the agent cannot see
features.plain: Tests the agent cannot see or edit decide whether an answer is right. A wrong "done" is caught, and the next helper is given the task plus the one failing line.
features.today: The checker code ships here and judged live fresh-clone runs.
features.exists: Validated on one kind of job (fix a bug, judged by hidden tests): in a recorded run of nine real jobs, seven answers were right the first time and two wrong "done" answers were caught. The checker's code ships in this repository, and it judged live fresh-clone runs that ended VERDICT PASS.
features.will: The same hidden tests judge every run, whichever coding tool runs it.
features.limit: One kind of job. The nine-job run used our earlier driver, so only the record of that run can be re-checked from here.

features.name: Works inside your harness
features.plain: ANIMA works inside the coding tool you already use (the harness): Muse Code first, then Claude Code, then Codex.
features.today: The Muse Code adapter runs one small bug task end to end.
features.exists: The Muse Code adapter runs one small bug task end to end: the worker fixes, the hidden checker judges, the record seals. Fresh-clone runs ended VERDICT PASS.
features.limit: Tiny task only. The tool must already be installed and logged in. The Claude Code and Codex adapters ship, but only Muse Code has a live pass in the merged tree.
features.expect: VERDICT PASS and CHAIN OK in a few minutes
features.needs: install first; Muse Code installed and logged in

features.name: Muse Code
features.plain: The first harness. Muse Code runs the task and ANIMA wraps it with the hidden checker and the rules.
features.exists: Ran live from a fresh clone: the worker fixed the bug and the hidden checker passed it (VERDICT PASS, about 100 seconds).
features.will: `anima run --harness muse --task tiny-bug` ends with `VERDICT PASS` and exit code 0.
features.limit: Tiny task only. The tool must already be installed and logged in.
features.expect: VERDICT PASS and CHAIN OK in a few minutes
features.needs: install first; Muse Code installed and logged in

features.name: Claude Code
features.plain: The second harness. The same task, sent to Claude Code, judged by the same hidden checker.
features.exists: The adapter ships in this repository. It ran the tiny task live in the earlier harness slice runs; in the merged tree it is dry-run only, which prints its exact command line.
features.will: `anima run --harness claude --task tiny-bug` ends with the checker's verdict.
features.limit: Tiny task only. The tool must already be installed and logged in.

features.name: Codex
features.plain: The third harness. The same task, sent to Codex, judged by the same hidden checker.
features.exists: The adapter ships in this repository. It ran the tiny task live in the earlier harness slice runs; in the merged tree it is dry-run only, which prints its exact command line.
features.will: `anima run --harness codex --task tiny-bug` ends with the checker's verdict.
features.limit: The run may end as NOT RUN if Codex is not installed and logged in on the machine. Tiny task only.

features.name: One line to install
features.plain: One command sets ANIMA up in a private folder, with no admin rights, then checks which of your coding tools it can find.
features.today: One line installs; `anima doctor` lists what it found.
features.exists: One line installs ANIMA into a private folder: the code, a small Python environment, a launcher, and a starter `anima.yaml` listing the coding tools it found. No admin rights, no passwords or keys asked.
features.limit: The coding tools must already be installed and logged in. Memory setup and voice each need one network download.
features.expect: ends with Installed. and the launcher path

features.name: One screen: the State Space Tree
features.plain: Every agent, task and attempt on one screen, drawn as a tree you can follow. SST stands for State Space Tree.
features.today: `anima status --tree` prints the tree; `anima ui` serves it as a page.
features.exists: `anima status --tree` prints the tree as text and `anima ui` serves the same tree as a page; both read the decision log, and `--demo` draws the built-in record with no run needed.
features.limit: It draws the decision log, not what a model is thinking. One computer. Command-file buttons stay disabled: no program reads them.

features.name: Talk to it
features.plain: Say what you want. Speech is turned into text on your own computer, with local Whisper.
features.today: Spoken commands run from a clip, with a confirm step.
features.exists: `anima voice` turns a clip into text on your own computer (local faster-whisper on the CPU, about 1 to 2 seconds a clip in the fresh-clone runs), matches one of six fixed commands, and asks before running anything.
features.limit: Six fixed English commands. Shown first from a recorded clip. Needs a Python with faster-whisper; the model downloads once.
features.expect: heard: Show status., matched: show status, dry run: not running it.
features.needs: install first; a Python with faster-whisper (set ANIMA_STT_PYTHON)

features.name: Roles and enforced rules
features.plain: Architect, manager and worker: who may do what, and rules a program enforces (secrets, no-push, budgets), written down once.
features.today: A design only, written down in docs/ROLES-AND-RULES.md. Nothing enforces it today.
features.exists: A design only, written down in docs/ROLES-AND-RULES.md with what exists marked. No program reads the file or enforces the rules today. The checker, the ladder and the record, which do exist in some form, are on the checker page.
features.will: One file, `anima.yaml`, holds roles, permissions, budgets, watches and the ladder, so it works on any harness.
features.limit: Designed from how we actually run our own work. Of the ten controls in the design, ANIMA has two today (the work ladder and the verification gate), and both are on the checker page.

features.name: Roles and a mission file
features.plain: Architect, manager, worker: who may do what, written in one file.
features.exists: The roles and the file format are written down as a design. No program reads the file today.
features.will: Each role gets a list of what it may do, what it must not do, and a budget. Every task card must point to a line of the mission and name a file as its test.

features.name: Rules that are enforced
features.plain: A small rule pack that blocks secrets, sudo, pushing to a public repository and deleting protected files. A program enforces it, not the agent's good intentions.
features.exists: We run a larger version of this on our own work. It is not part of ANIMA today.
features.will: `anima check --cmd 'cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519'` prints `block` and exits with code 3.
features.limit: Blocking before the action runs is proven only on Claude Code, which has per-action hooks. Budgets are in the design, not in this first pack.

features.name: A wrong answer climbs to a stronger helper
features.plain: When the checker says no, the next helper gets the task plus the one failing line: a Muse Code worker first (in the recorded runs), then Claude Sonnet, then Codex.
features.exists: The ladder code ships in this repository. In the recorded run both wrong answers went one rung up to Claude Sonnet, which fixed them. The Codex rung was not needed.
features.will: The ladder runs inside every run across the harnesses you have installed.
features.limit: The second helper was told the failing line, so it was an informed retry, not a blind one. One run, nine jobs.

features.name: A record nobody can quietly edit
features.plain: Every decision is one line in a log, and each line carries a fingerprint of the line before it, so an edit shows.
features.exists: The 69-record log of the nine-job run, a checker script anyone can run in a second, and a page that does the same check in your browser.
features.limit: The seal shows the record was not changed afterwards. It cannot show that the run itself was honest. The check does not re-run the nine jobs.
features.expect: recorded run: CHAIN OK - 69 records, every link matches, then: edited copy: CHAIN BROKEN - 69 records, line 7 does not match the line before it
features.needs: Python 3 and git; about 11 MB; about one second
